LANDING.HERO_DESC: Group chat and group calling for the platform. Messages take a durable REST path and arrive over a WebSocket; calls are hand-built on RTCPeerConnection — perfect negotiation, trickle ICE, a TURN relay and a peer-to-peer mesh — rather than handed to a media SDK, because building that by hand is the point of this product.
LANDING.HERO_STATUS: Everything below is running, not planned. Conversations, groups, read receipts, image attachments, presence and typing; audio and video calls up to four people over a mesh, with screen share, a focusable call stage and call history in the thread; and chat windows you can dock over any page of the platform. What is deliberately not built is an SFU — a mesh holds about four, and the room model an SFU needs already exists, so that stays a later phase rather than a rewrite.
LANDING.CARD_ANGULAR: Angular 21 with signals and strict TypeScript, federated into the shell. This remote exposes two modules: `./Module` for the routed product at `/messenger`, and `./HeaderWidget` for the icon in the shell header.
LANDING.CARD_HEADER_WIDGET: An ambient product cannot live behind a route — it needs a socket, a badge and ringing on every page. The shell renders the widget from an `environment.headerWidgets` entry and never imports messenger code; if this remote is down the slot stays empty and the header still works.
LANDING.CARD_WEBRTC: RTCPeerConnection driven directly: perfect negotiation (polite/impolite peers) to kill glare bugs, trickle ICE so candidates flow as they are found, and DTLS-SRTP encryption the browser does for free. Screen share is a second track added by renegotiation, never a replacement for the camera.
LANDING.CARD_AUTH: angular-oauth2-oidc with PKCE; Google and Microsoft sign-in through the Go gateway, which mints the internal JWT every service trusts.
LANDING.CARD_REALTIME: One Go service holding one WebSocket per browser: presence, typing, signalling relay and TURN credentials. Split from the chat store on purpose — ten thousand idle sockets and durable message history have opposite scaling profiles.
LANDING.CARD_NATS_CORE: Live frames fan out over core NATS on `rt.owner.<owner_id>`, so any socket instance can serve any user and no sticky sessions are needed. Core, not JetStream: a durable consumer would redeliver stale chat frames on every reconnect.
LANDING.CARD_COTURN: A relay for the 10-20% of calls that symmetric NAT and corporate firewalls block. Credentials are HMAC-derived and expire in minutes, so a stolen bundle cannot rent our bandwidth; coturn forwards ciphertext it cannot read.
LANDING.CARD_MESSENGER_SERVICE: Fastify + TypeScript owning conversations, groups, messages, receipts and call history. Sending is REST, never a socket write: a durable write must be retriable and idempotent. A conversation sorts on its own `last_activity_at`, advanced by both the message transaction and the call projection — because a call is activity too, and a column named after messages could only ever lie about that.
LANDING.CARD_ACCOUNTS: The platform's user directory, live on :3006. Upserts your profile from the gateway's identity headers after login and answers directory search — Messenger needs to know who you can talk to before a conversation can exist.
LANDING.CARD_POSTGRES: Message history, conversation membership and receipts. The boring, transactional half of the product — and the half you never want a signalling deploy to endanger.
LANDING.CARD_JETSTREAM: Every domain event is also published to the `EVENTS` stream, so event-store keeps the record and other services can project from it. The log and the wire are deliberately different transports.

MESSAGE_FLOW.SUBTITLE: A message is written once, durably, then fanned out to live sockets. Tap any step for detail.
MESSAGE_FLOW.DIAGRAM_ARIA: Message flow, from composer to recipient
MESSAGE_FLOW.PANEL_EMPTY: Select a step in the diagram to see what happens there.
MESSAGE_FLOW.NOTE: Receiving is a socket; sending never is. A write with no durability behind it is not a sent message.

COMPOSER.TITLE: Composer (browser)
COMPOSER.DESC: The remote posts the message over HTTP with an idempotency key.
COMPOSER.D1: REST, so the write is retriable
COMPOSER.D2: Retry on failure is safe — same key, same message
COMPOSER.D3: No optimistic write is treated as delivered

SERVICE.TITLE: messenger-service
SERVICE.DESC: Validates membership, stamps the sender from the gateway header, and stores.
SERVICE.D1: Identity comes from the trusted header, never the body
SERVICE.D2: Authorization via can(subject, action, resource) — OPA later
SERVICE.D3: Duplicate idempotency key returns the original message

POSTGRES.TITLE: PostgreSQL
POSTGRES.DESC: The message becomes history the moment the transaction commits.
POSTGRES.D1: Durable before anyone is told it exists
POSTGRES.D2: Receipts and membership live beside it
POSTGRES.D3: Pagination and search read from here, not from the socket

NATS.TITLE: NATS — log and wire
NATS.DESC: One event, two transports: JetStream for the record, core for delivery.
NATS.D1: JetStream EVENTS → event-store keeps the 90-day log
NATS.D2: Core NATS carries the live frame with no replay
NATS.D3: A durable consumer here would resend stale chat on reconnect

REALTIME.TITLE: realtime-service
REALTIME.DESC: Subscribes per connected user and pushes the frame down their socket.
REALTIME.D1: Subject per owner, so any instance can serve any user
REALTIME.D2: Presence and typing ride the same connection
REALTIME.D3: No database on this path — sockets stay cheap

RECIPIENT.TITLE: Recipient (browser)
RECIPIENT.DESC: The frame updates the open thread and the header badge.
RECIPIENT.D1: Badge counts unread conversations, not messages
RECIPIENT.D2: A duplicate frame is harmless — the badge is a set
RECIPIENT.D3: Cleared when the thread is open and the tab is focused

CALL_FLOW.SUBTITLE: Signalling goes through our server; media does not. Tap any step for detail.
CALL_FLOW.DIAGRAM_ARIA: WebRTC call setup, from credentials to connected media
CALL_FLOW.PANEL_EMPTY: Select a step in the diagram to see what happens there.
CALL_FLOW.NOTE: The server relays offers and candidates; audio and video flow directly between the two browsers.

CREDENTIALS.TITLE: TURN credentials
CREDENTIALS.DESC: Before dialling, the browser asks the gateway for short-lived relay credentials.
CREDENTIALS.D1: Valid for minutes, issued per call
CREDENTIALS.D2: username = expiry:owner_id, password = HMAC of it
CREDENTIALS.D3: The TURN secret never leaves the server

OFFER.TITLE: Offer / answer
OFFER.DESC: Each side builds an RTCPeerConnection and describes what it can send.
OFFER.D1: Perfect negotiation: one polite peer, one impolite
OFFER.D2: Glare is resolved by rollback, not by retry loops
OFFER.D3: getUserMedia needs a secure context — localhost counts

RELAY.TITLE: Signalling relay
RELAY.DESC: realtime-service passes SDP and ICE between the two participants.
RELAY.D1: The server stamps who sent the frame
RELAY.D2: A frame is relayed only between call participants
RELAY.D3: A client-supplied sender field is never trusted

ICE.TITLE: Trickle ICE
ICE.DESC: Candidates are exchanged as they are discovered rather than in one batch.
ICE.D2: STUN finds the public address behind NAT

MEDIA.TITLE: Media, peer to peer
MEDIA.DESC: Audio and video flow directly between browsers once a pair connects.
MEDIA.D1: DTLS-SRTP encryption is not optional in WebRTC
MEDIA.D2: 1:1 is a mesh; an SFU arrives at five participants
MEDIA.D3: Navigating to another app must not drop the call

TURN.TITLE: TURN relay (fallback)
TURN.DESC: When no direct path exists, coturn forwards the encrypted stream.
TURN.D1: Symmetric NAT and strict firewalls need this
TURN.D2: The relay cannot read what it forwards
TURN.D3: Without it, 10-20% of real calls simply fail

LANDING.CARD_MESH: A group call is N-1 peer connections per person, not a server in the middle — so each browser uploads its camera once per peer and the room costs O(N²) links overall. That is what caps it at four. Who offers in each pair is the lexicographically lower owner id (Matrix MSC3401's rule), because two people joining in the same instant each see the other as the newcomer.
LANDING.CARD_ROOM: A call is a room: an invited set resolved from conversation membership and never widened, plus a joined set. Every signalling frame names its target and is checked against that invited set, which is what makes ringing a stranger impossible. Instances heartbeat and a reaper closes calls whose holder died, because a state machine closed only by the process most likely to crash is permanently wrong the first time that happens.
